notes: One fixed scale, camera, canvas and pivot for every frame of a unit - never recentred or rescaled per pose.

These are real, working numbers from a shipped project's sprite pipeline, kept as a starting point - not a spec to match blindly. Re-derive px_per_m and the canvas size against your own reference (see docs/SPRITES.md); everything else here is a reasonable default.
Pivot: the projected ground origin (0, 0, ground_z); every frame renders on the same canvas with the pivot on the same whole pixel.

lighting.note: key and fill are area (disk) lights aimed at target_m unless rotation_euler is given instead of aim; world is a flat background colour/strength (ambient fill). Re-tune all of it by eye against your own reference - there is nothing universal about these particular numbers beyond that they worked for one 1.75 m tall figure.

readability.note: thin rigid parts (a shaft, a bowstring) can vanish at small on-screen sizes. Scale just that material's faces radially about the object's own axis, on a render-only copy - never the approved model. One entry per thin part.

shadow.note: a flat silhouette of every rendered mesh except `exclude_objects`, sheared by (shear_x * height_above_ground, shear_y * height_above_ground) to suggest a low sun angle, rasterised at `supersample` x and downsampled, then composited under the beauty pass at `alpha`/255.
shadow.exclude_note: anything that shouldn't cast a shadow of its own - a held weapon here, or something that already lies flat on the ground

mask.note: a second, Raw-view render with one flat-emission override material, so a game engine gets clean per-pixel channel data with no tone-mapping or anti-aliasing colour bleed. Red is team colour (below). Green here is measured from the game, not invented: SHCDE's own Unlit/TeamColour shader reads a second, height-based value from this same mask for a lower-sprite cutaway effect (docs/SHCDE.md section 7) - green = clamp(round(green_channel.intercept + green_channel.slope_per_px x (image_row - pivot_row_from_top)), 0, 255), top-origin rows. If your target engine doesn't use a channel like this, drop `green_channel` and green stays 0.

team_colour.note: which part(s) carry team/variant colour is a design decision for your own project.
team_colour.region_forms: each region is {object, material} (faces using that material slot) or {object, vertex_group, min_weight} (faces whose vertices all carry at least min_weight)
team_colour.neutral_note: a multiply-based team-colour shader needs its target faces bright and neutral in the beauty render, or no tint shows once multiplied: grey = neutral_albedo x the face's own luminance / its texture's mean luminance.

checks.note: optional per-frame measurements, geometric (from the 3D scene) and pixel (from the rendered mask), that tools/validate_sprites.py compares against each other as a sanity check - see docs/SPRITES.md section 9 and docs/SHCDE.md section 10.

facing_side_rule.note: measured from the game's own Hoplite-carrier example: at the front facing the tracked object reads on screen-right, at the back facing it reads on screen-left, and it should read larger/nearer at the left-profile facing than the right-profile one. Written for an object worn on the character's left; mirror the signs for one on the right.
